subject: maths
title: Area of composite shapes and trapeziums

lines.say: A trapezium has exactly one pair of parallel sides. Call them a and b.
lines.alt: Trapezium with parallel sides a and b and height h

lines.say: The height h is measured at right angles to the parallel sides.
Add the parallel, times the tall, halve it all.
Here is a trapezium. Top 6, bottom 10, height 5.
Copy it and turn the copy upside down. Slide them together.

draw.alt: A second, upside-down trapezium joins to form a parallelogram

lines.say: Together they make a shape 16 wide and 5 high. That's 80.
The trapezium is half of it. So its area is 40 square centimetres.
Check: the average width is 8. 8 times 5 is 40.
A kite's diagonals cross at right angles.
Draw a box around it. The kite fills exactly half the box.
lines.alt: Kite with diagonals 8 and 6 inside an 8 by 6 rectangle

lines.say: Diagonals 8 and 6. Half of 8 times 6 is 24.
This L-shaped floor is 14 by 10, with a 6 by 4 corner missing.

draw.alt: 14 by 10 rectangle with a 6 by 4 corner

lines.say: Big rectangle first. 14 times 10 is 140.
Take away the missing corner. 6 times 4 is 24.
Check by adding pieces. 84 plus 32 is 116. Two ways, one answer.
A pool 10 by 6 has a 2 metre path all around.
lines.alt: Pool with a 2 m path around it

lines.say: The path adds 2 on both ends. So the outside is 14 by 10.
Take away the pool, 60. The path is 80 square metres.
Working backwards: a trapezium has area 63, sides 8 and 10. Find h.
Half of 18 is 9. 9 times h is 63, so h is 7.
Don't forget the half in the trapezium formula.
A sloping side is never the height.
Borders go both ways. Add the width twice.
Convert units before you multiply.
Trapezium: average width times height.
Kite and rhombus: diagonals times, then halve.
Composite: add the pieces, or subtract from the big box.
